stem.text: Classify the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(-1\right)^{n + 1}}{\left(n + 1\right)^{2}} \) as absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent.

answer_key.label: The series converges absolutely, because the series of absolute values converges by comparison with a p-series.

worked_solution.text: Test the series of absolute values, \( \sum \frac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)^{2}} \). By limit comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), the ratio of terms tends to \( 1 \), a positive finite number.
That p-series has p = \( 2 \) > 1 and converges, so the series of absolute values converges and the given series converges absolutely.

options.label: The series diverges, because the series of absolute values is compared with a p-series.
options.derivation: the conclusion drawn about a series it does not name

options.label: The series converges conditionally, because the series of absolute values converges by comparison with a p-series.
options.derivation: the absolute and conditional labels exchanged

options.label: The series converges conditionally, because it passes the alternating series test.
options.derivation: absolute values omitted, so the absolute series was never tested and only the alternating series test was used

options.label: The series converges absolutely, because the series of absolute values converges by comparison with a p-series.
